newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods advance, Gulf gasoline shines.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods advance, Gulf gasoline shines.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices advanced on the shoulders of NYMEX futures and mostly firmer differentials late Wednesday, with Gulf conventional gasoline shining especially bright amid short-covering ahead of tomorrow's Thanksgiving holiday.
Prompt back-34th-cycle Gulf "M4" grade conventional unleaded was offered at 0.25 cent below December futures, one cent firmer than Tuesday diffs, players said.
"A few big players came onto the scene after noon," a Gulf trader said, including a Wall Street trading firm -- breaking the monotony of sleepy activity earlier in the day.

New York Harbor reformulated "A5" grade gasoline was sold for 5.50 cents above the print, also about one cent firmer than Tuesday differentials, helped by EIA inventory data showing a 1.3 million barrel draw on total U.S. gasoline stocks for the prior week.
The report was more bullish than Tuesday's API report, which estimated a 637,000 barrel total draw on gasoline.
Distillate diffs were steady to higher, with New York Harbor heating oil offered at about 0.15 cent below the print and Gulf material at 3.0 cents under, traders said.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
